semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: 'Medical simulation' closely relates to the use of virtual reality as both pertain to creating simulated environments for educational, training, or treatment purposes in medicine.
'Simulation in surgical training' is another form of virtual reality utilized specifically for surgical practice, matching the core idea of virtual environments applied to medicine.

parent_domains.justification: This domain acts as a broader category inclusive of virtual reality as it focuses on educational aspects involving simulation which VR is commonly used for.
This encompasses the broader application of technology, such as VR, within medical settings, thus acting as a parent domain.
This is the broadest category under which all medical-related domains fall, including virtual reality applications.
Since VR could involve dynamic simulations enhanced by AI capabilities in medical contexts, this domain acts as a parent.
This pertains to the general field within which virtual reality applications in medicine lie.
This involves using computational technologies, including virtual simulations like VR, to address medical challenges.

closest_parent_domain.justification: As virtual reality is fundamentally a tool used primarily for immersive educational and training simulations in medical fields, this domain most closely encapsulates its application.

child_domains.justification: A specific application of virtual reality within the realm of surgery, this domain represents a narrower focus under broader virtual reality applications.

closest_child_domain.justification: This child domain specifically addresses a critical and focused niche within medical simulation using VR, namely surgical training.

sibling_domains.justification: While virtual reality is specific to immersive environments, using AI in medical education aligns closely under the same parent of educational technology.
This domain, while different, is another specialized field that falls under broad medical applications, sharing a sibling relationship.
Virtual reality as a tool may parallel other specialized medical equipment, both serving as siblings in broader medical technology categories.
Both virtual reality and digital health are intertwined as technical solutions within modern healthcare systems.
Serves similar ends in facilitating medical processes, although through a variety of technologies.
Being another specialized application of technology in medical treatments, this domain shares a sibling status in wide medical applications.
While virtual reality is used more for simulation, both fall under technological advancements in healthcare, being siblings under broader medical technology umbrellas.
This domain represents broad structural and operational applications in healthcare that VR could support, rendering them siblings.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: 'Digital health' is closely related as it also embraces advanced technologies like VR for transformative impacts in healthcare settings, emphasizing the digital aspect just like VR.

unrelated_domains.justification: Virology, being a study of viruses, is not influenced or directly related to virtual reality technologies.
This domain, while tangentially related, focuses on subjective patient outcomes and experiences, which is not directly what VR targets.
